The Cleveland Cavaliers are an American professional basketball team.
The Cleveland Cavaliers compete in the National Basketball Association (NBA).
The Cleveland Cavaliers are based in Cleveland.
The Cleveland Cavaliers began play as an expansion team in 1970.
The Portland Trail Blazers and Buffalo Braves were also expansion teams that began play in 1970.
The Cleveland Cavaliers' home games were first held at Cleveland Arena from 1970 to 1974.
The Cleveland Cavaliers' home games were then played at the Richfield Coliseum from 1974 to 1994.
Since 1994, the Cleveland Cavaliers have played home games at Rocket Mortgage FieldHouse in downtown Cleveland.
Dan Gilbert has owned the team since March 2005.
The Cleveland Cavaliers opened their inaugural season by losing their first 15 games.
The Cleveland Cavaliers struggled in their early years, placing no better than sixth in the Eastern Conference during their first five seasons.
The Cleveland Cavaliers won their first Central Division title in 1976.
The 1976 team was led by Austin Carr, Bobby "Bingo" Smith, Jim Chones, Dick Snyder, Nate Thurmond and head coach Bill Fitch.
The "Miracle at Richfield" occurred when the Cavaliers defeated the Washington Bullets, 4–3, in the Eastern Conference Semifinals.
In Game 7 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals, the Cavaliers won 87–85 with a shot by Snyder with four seconds to go.
After winning their first Central Division title in 1976, the Cavaliers advanced to the Eastern Conference Finals for the first time.
The Cleveland Cavaliers were without Chones after he broke his toe before the series opener against the Boston Celtics.
The Cleveland Cavaliers lost the Eastern Conference Finals to the Boston Celtics, 4–2.
The Cleveland Cavaliers made playoff appearances in the following two seasons.
The Cleveland Cavaliers had a six-year playoff drought.
LeBron James was the first overall pick of the 2003 NBA draft and is a forward for the Cavaliers.

LeBron James is a perennial NBA All-Star.
LeBron James has won four-time NBA MVP.
LeBron James led the team to its first NBA Finals in 2007.
LeBron James led the team to their first championship in 2016.
Ted Stepien purchased the franchise in 1980.
During Stepien's tenure, the Cavaliers made a practice of trading future draft picks for marginal veteran players.
The most notable deal during Stepien's ownership sent a 1982 first-round pick to the Los Angeles Lakers in exchange for Don Ford and the 22nd overall pick in 1980.
As a result of Stepien's dealings, the NBA introduced the "Stepien Rule", which prohibits teams from trading first-round draft picks in successive seasons.
The Cavaliers went 66–180 during Stepien's three years as owner.
During Stepien's ownership, the Cavaliers dropped to the bottom of the league in attendance and lost $15 million.
The Cavaliers went through six coaches during this span, including four during the 1981–82 season.
The team finished 15–67 during the 1981–82 season.
Between March and November 1982, the team had a 24-game losing streak, which was the NBA's longest at the time.
George and Gordon Gund purchased the Cavaliers from Stepien in 1983.
The Cavaliers made the playoffs 10 times between 1985 and 1998.

The 1988–89 season was the Cavaliers' best season to date, finishing the regular season at 57–25 with a team that included Brad Daugherty, Mark Price, Ron Harper and Larry Nance, and head coach Lenny Wilkens.
The 1988–89 season also saw the Cavaliers have their second 57-win season in 1991–92 and reach the Eastern Conference Finals that year.
Between 1999 and 2005, the Cavaliers failed to make a playoff appearance.
The Cavaliers finished the 2002–03 season with a record of 17–65, tied for the worst in the NBA.
The Cavaliers had the No. 1 pick in the 2003 NBA draft and selected LeBron James.
On January 3, 2005, the team was sold to businessman Dan Gilbert for $375 million.
That year, the team also hired head coach Mike Brown and general manager Danny Ferry.
The Cavaliers built a team around James and Žydrūnas Ilgauskas by adding players such as Drew Gooden, Larry Hughes and Anderson Varajao.
Under this new leadership, the Cavaliers made five straight playoffs from 2006 to 2010, advancing to at least the second round each time.
The 2006–07 Cavaliers advanced to the franchise's first NBA Finals but were swept by the San Antonio Spurs.
The 2008–09 Cavaliers won a franchise-record 66 games and had a franchise-best 39–2 record at home, but lost the Eastern Conference Finals to the Orlando Magic.
Despite the addition of four-time NBA champion Shaquille O'Neal, the 2009–10 Cavaliers were unable to return to the Eastern Conference Finals after losing to the Boston Celtics in the second round.
With the Cavaliers out of the playoffs, the focus turned to James' impending free agency.
On July 8, 2010, LeBron James announced that he would be signing with the Miami Heat in a nationally televised one-hour special titled The Decision.
The repercussions of this announcement left many in Cleveland feeling betrayed and infuriated.
After a 19–win season in 2010–11, the Cavaliers began a rebuild around Kyrie Irving, whom they selected first overall in the 2011 NBA draft.
In 2014, LeBron James returned to the Cavaliers after four seasons with the Miami Heat.
While the Miami Heat had a 224–88 record during James' four-year tenure and won NBA titles in 2012 and 2013, the Cavaliers went 97–215 and missed the playoffs each season.
The Cavaliers made several moves to build a championship-contending team around James, most notably acquiring power forward Kevin Love from the Minnesota Timberwolves.
With this "Big Three" of James, Love and Irving, the Lebron-led Cavaliers made four consecutive Finals appearances from 2015 to 2018 – all against the Golden State Warriors – winning in 2016.
The 2016 NBA Championship marked the first title in franchise history for the Cavaliers as they became the first team to come back from a 3–1 deficit to win the Finals.
It was also Cleveland's first championship in major professional sports since 1964, ending the so-called Cleveland sports curse.
The Cavaliers' roster went through many changes in the 2017–18 season, most notably the trade of Irving to the Boston Celtics in exchange for Isaiah Thomas and other assets.
Thomas was later traded to the Los Angeles Lakers as part of a trade deadline overhaul that saw the Cavaliers add Jordan Clarkson, Larry Nance Jr. (son of Cavs legend Larry Nance) and others.
The following offseason, James declined his player option to rejoin the team, instead signing with the Lakers.
In the following two seasons, the team recorded only 19 wins and failed to make the playoffs.

In the first three seasons since James left the second time, the Cavaliers won a total of 60 games, missed the playoffs each season and had four different head coaches: Tyronn Lue, Larry Drew, John Beilein and current head coach J.B. Bickerstaff.
In the 2021–22 season, the Cavs finished 44–38 and eighth in the Eastern Conference, qualifying for the NBA play-in tournament for the first time since 2017–18.
This also marked the team's first postseason basketball since 2017–18 and the first time a non-LeBron-led team qualified for postseason play since 1997–98.
The team, however, did not make it out of the play-in tournament, losing to the Brooklyn Nets and then to the Atlanta Hawks, ending their season.
On March 26, 2023, Myles Garrett purchased a minority ownership stake in the Cavaliers and would serve as an ambassador for the team.
The Cavaliers qualified for the 2024 NBA Playoffs as the 4th seed in the Eastern Conference.
In the first round of the playoffs, the Cavaliers defeated the Orlando Magic 4–3 but lost to the Boston Celtics 4–1 in the Conference semifinals.
